title: Undetermined Coefficients
body:
The guess-and-match method for the particular solution $y_p$ of a [[Non-Homogeneous ODE]]. Guess
that $y_p$ has the same *shape* as the forcing term, with unknown constants in it, substitute, and
solve for the constants by matching coefficients.

It works because polynomials, exponentials, and sines and cosines all stay in their own family when
differentiated. It fails for anything that does not, $\ln t$ or $1/t$ or $\tan t$, and variation of
parameters is the fallback.

| Forcing term $f(t)$ | Guess $y_p$ |
|---|---|
| $e^{kt}$ | $Ae^{kt}$ |
| polynomial of degree $n$ | full polynomial $A_nt^n + \dots + A_0$ |
| $\sin kt$ or $\cos kt$ | $A\cos kt + B\sin kt$, **both terms** |
| product of the above | product of the guesses |

Two rules that cause most of the lost marks:

- **Use the full polynomial.** $f(t) = t^2$ needs $At^2 + Bt + C$, not $At^2$
- **Include both sine and cosine**, even if only one appears in $f$. Differentiating produces the
  other one

## The collision rule

If any term of the guess already appears in the complementary solution $y_c$, it solves the
homogeneous equation and substituting it gives $0 = f(t)$. **Multiply the guess by $t$** (or $t^2$
for a doubly repeated root) and try again. Same repair as the repeated-root case in
[[Homogeneous ODE]], for the same reason, and physically it is resonance.

```
y'' - 3y' + 2y = e^t

y_c = c₁eᵗ + c₂e²ᵗ           roots r = 1, 2
guess Aeᵗ                    collides with c₁eᵗ
use  Ateᵗ  instead           →  A = -1,  y_p = -teᵗ
```

## Related

- [[Non-Homogeneous ODE]]: what this is a step of
- [[Homogeneous ODE]]: solve it first, you need $y_c$ to check for collisions
- [[Cauchy-Euler]]: reduces to a constant-coefficient equation, then finishes here
